title: Pansy Lane's band and his Pluto Blues
summary: Pansy's band at Thomas E and anecdotes, including a stranded sailboat and a distinctive loud horn.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: What about the Rosenmiles? I don't know. Tom Early, you remember Tom Early, bass player? No. He had the Triangle, no, it wasn't a Triangle, what was his name, Harmony, huh? I can't remember Tom Early's band. Raymond worked with him, anyway. And the Rosenmiles.

Oh, who was in Pansy Lane's band? Pansy? Well, the Molos were there again. You had, uh, Molos playing drum. You had, uh, his brother playing trombone. Cats playing drum. No, no, Molos, no, Cats was playing drum. Let's see, who the heck was in that band? Raymond was playing clarinet, when I remember. Uh, I don't know, I can't recall, Dick, but I know Raymond was playing clarinet, Pansy was playing trumpet, Cats was on drums, and I think Molos, well, I better not say, I don't know who was playing trumpet. No. But Cats, uh, or Raymond could tell you better than I can. Where did you hear him? Well, I used to go sit in with him over the river at Thomas E's just for kicks. After I quit playing, you know, I told you I laid my horn up, now and then I'd go get a, have a, a yin to play, I'd go sit in with, tell Cats, well, Cats pick me up tonight, I'm gonna go over the river with you. On a Saturday night, they played Thomas E's over there. And it was a picture show to, to listen to Pansy, man, to get your kicks with him, things he'd come up with, you know.
Touch and, what would he do? Oh.

He used to carry one, one of those things, you know, you, you blow and it'd go, tch, tch, tch. Yeah. And carry that around, you do that at the people, off the bandstand. He was a character, man. Was that the Pluto blues? Yeah. Yeah, well, he composed the Pluto blues. Yeah, he composed that. He was a character.
What was that like, the Pluto blues? I don't remember.

Him and Cats got lost at Biloxi one day, you know, they got out in one of these sailboats. They took two girls out in the sailboats and the wind blew them way offshore, see. And a storm come up, and this girl and Cats were getting, they were frightened, you know. And Pansy had his horn out there. And the Cat says he took that horn, and he started blowing it. He says he finally drew people's attention on the shore with that horn. He says he could, he could really hit the loudest note on the horn I ever hear anybody blow, man. Mm-hmm. He'd blow you off the bandstand if you felt like it. Mm-hmm.
He didn't like you to call him Pansy, man. If you called him Pansy, like Pansy, he'd know you. He'd start swinging at you. Mm-hmm .
